text:
emma_support: FYI escalation from a paying customer — after they pinned to our embed-768 variant they started getting 1536-dim vectors intermittently. They say it happens only on batched calls (batch_size > 1). Attaching sample.

raj_engineering: can you paste the minimal request + one response? also what model id exactly did they pin to? :eyes:

emma_support: pinned to `redwood/embedding-lite@v2.3.1` (customer pin). Example request they sent:

```http
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "redwood/embedding-lite@v2.3.1",
  "input": ["doc A", "doc B"],
  "batch_size": 2,
  "batch_pad": true
}
```

Response (truncated):
```json
{
  "data": [
    { "embedding": [ /* 1536 floats... */ ] },
    { "embedding": [ /* 1536 floats... */ ] }
  ]
}
```

They also repro'ed locally by sending two short strings in one request and saw 1536, but a single-item request returns 768 as expected.

sophie_sre: interesting — only when batch_pad is true? any difference if they set batch_size 2 but pad=false?

emma_support: customer said pad=false still gave the problem in their initial runs, but their SDK defaults to pad=true so initial reports showed pad=true.

raj_engineering: quick hypothesis — runtime may be concatenating two embeddings when a batched request hits a fallback path that merges results from two different model variants (legacy 1536-vec variant + 768-vec variant). Need logs from the serving runtime for that request id. can you ask customer for request-id or X-Request-ID header? also check routing headers like `X-Model-Variant` in our ingress logs.

mike_oncall: adding oncall to thread. If it's a variant-mix routing bug we should check recent canaries/variant substitution rules — might be a mapping mismatch introduced in the v2.3.1 pin behavior. deploy-bot, any recent rollout affecting embed variants?

deploy-bot: [deploy-notice] 2026-02-26T04:12Z - Canary rollout of variant-refactor (model routing) to us-west-2. Revision r-20260225. No hard switches yet; fallback routing tests enabled on ~5% traffic.

raj_engineering: that aligns. If fallback merging is enabled on canary, a batched request could be split internally and get responses from two variants then be concatenated incorrectly. Can you grab a sample X-Request-ID and the corresponding runtime log lines showing model name / variant used and response sizes? look for lines like `ServingVariant:` and `embedding_len=`.

emma_support: customer provided request-id `req_8b9c3f`. Pasted runtime logs they pulled from their side (they forwarded our proxy logs):

```
[ingress] req=req_8b9c3f route=redwood/embedding-lite@v2.3.1 -> routed_variant=embed-legacy-1536
[serve] req=req_8b9c3f chunk=0 variant=embed-legacy-1536 embedding_len=1536
[serve] req=req_8b9c3f chunk=1 variant=embed-lite-768 embedding_len=768
[assemble] req=req_8b9c3f fused_embeddings=1536
```

That looks like two different variants were used for different chunks and then the assembler fused them.

raj_engineering: confirmed — bug in the batch assembler where it assumes all chunk responses share the same vector width and in mismatch cases it concatenates rather than erroring. Repro steps for engineering: send a batched request that hits split-by-chunk routing across variants; verify assembler behavior.

mike_oncall: mitigation for customers: temporarily set `batch_size=1` or pin to an explicit variant name that has 768 only (not the abstract alias) until we have a fix. Also we can disable the canary fallback for this customer (per-tenant routing override) if needed.

emma_support: I'll relay mitigations. Customer asked: is this data-lossy or could embeddings be silently wrong at scale? they rely on vector store indexing.

sophie_sre: it's silent corruption for any item that was produced from mixed-variant assembly — downstream index will have wrong vec size. Recommend we mark all recent customer writes with that request id range as suspect and offer reindex assistance.

raj_engineering: plan: 1) patch assembler to validate uniform dim and throw an error if mismatch (hotfix), 2) add a telemetry alert when assembler encounters mixed dims, 3) backfill a daily job to find suspect writes by checking vector length metadata. I'll open an internal PR and a runbook.

emma_support: customer is asking for ETA — can you estimate hotfix timeline? they want to resume batched uploads.

raj_engineering: hotfix to return errors by default — ~4 hours to code+test+canary (small change), full rollback/patch across regions ~12-24h if no regressions. I'll start the PR now and request expedited review.

mike_oncall: I'll add the tenant to the routing override to force single-variant routing until patch is live. :thumbsup:

emma_support: thanks team. I'll update customer with workaround and our remediation plan. will post updates here once the PR is merged and rollback applied. :white_check_mark:
